title: GraphQL Subscriptions
description: Explore real-time data with GraphQL subscriptions (post-MVP)

questions.explanation: A subscription is a long-lived connection that pushes real-time data updates to the client when specific events occur.

questions.text: How do subscriptions differ from queries?
questions.explanation: Queries fetch data once, subscriptions establish persistent connections that push updates when data changes.
questions.hint: One is push, one is pull

questions.text: What transport is used for GraphQL subscriptions?
questions.explanation: WebSockets are typically used for subscriptions to maintain persistent, bidirectional communication.

questions.text: What are common use cases for subscriptions?
questions.explanation: Live notifications, chat messages, real-time dashboards, activity feeds, and collaborative editing are common examples.

questions.text: Do subscriptions require special client libraries?
questions.explanation: Yes, clients need support for WebSocket connections and subscription lifecycle management, not all HTTP clients can handle this.
